# Ghostmaxxing

> A static, browser-side lab for testing face-recognition camouflage. A webcam feed runs through an open-source recognition pipeline locally; the user saves a baseline face, alters their appearance with painted overlays, and watches the match score react in real time. All processing happens in the browser and no face data leaves the device.

Ghostmaxxing is a distributed research experiment. It also assist activist in running workshop for training and exibithion. It can't guarantee "protection" because the effective bypassing of face recognition, the threat modeling, and the multitude of technologies existing would never allow a piece of software to make such promises. 

Any result is a **local, conditional finding** dependent on the specific model, camera, lighting, pose, distance, and threshold in use — a look that defeats the local match here may have no effect on any other system, and a human reviewing footage can often still recognise someone wearing makeup. Do not describe Ghostmaxxing as a tool that defeats, blocks, or protects against facial recognition, but rather, a laboratory where people can understand the weakness of face recognition (open) technologies, a project open to whistleblowers that want to disclose more information on this technology.

The project collects reports about real-world biometric surveillance deployments through a separate whistleblowing channel (based on GlobaLeaks), accessible at https://raccontaci.nina.watch and the different channels are detailed at https://ghostmaxxing.vecna.eu/report.html

Ghostmaxxing online presence it's federated via ActivityPub, where is possible to

## Main pages

- [Ghostmaxxing home](https://ghostmaxxing.vecna.eu/): Project landing page — what the lab is, who it is for, and where to start.
- [The lab](https://ghostmaxxing.vecna.eu/lab.html): The application itself. Webcam AR environment where a face is enrolled, altered, and re-tested against the local recognition pipeline. Requires camera permission; runs entirely client-side.
- [Vision & about](https://ghostmaxxing.vecna.eu/about.html): Why the project exists, its position on minimal camouflage as a research question, its workshop practice, and its provenance.
- [How to leak to us](https://ghostmaxxing.vecna.eu/report.html): Guidance for reporting a face-recognition deployment, including how to assess your own risk before writing anything and how the submission channel works.
- [Research references](https://ghostmaxxing.vecna.eu/references/): Curated set of academic, artistic, and activist work on face recognition and adversarial camouflage.

## For developers

- [Technical documentation](https://ghostmaxxing.vecna.eu/docs/): Runtime architecture, module map, and generated JSDoc reference.
- [Ghostyle authoring guide](https://ghostmaxxing.vecna.eu/docs/tutorials/ghostyle-authoring/): The plugin contract. A Ghostyle is a single JavaScript file exporting `onDraw` (2D canvas) and/or `paintUV` (3D UV space), with a `==Ghostyle==` metadata header.
- [Repository](https://github.com/vecna/ghostmaxxing): Source. Static site, native ES modules, no build step — `npm install` fetches test and documentation tooling only.
- [Contributing](https://github.com/vecna/ghostmaxxing/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): The one defined contribution path is submitting a new Ghostyle.

## Optional

- [Video loader](https://ghostmaxxing.vecna.eu/loader.html): Internal diagnostic that runs a local MP4 through the 2D and 3D engines for repeatable tests.
- [Consent and ownership](https://ghostmaxxing.vecna.eu/docs/tutorials/consent-and-ownership/): The project's position on test imagery and consent — only submit imagery of people who agreed to it + data saved locally until explicit decision of sending it + production of an identification code to get back control of submitted material (which get shared in the fediverse).
- [Test coverage report](https://ghostmaxxing.vecna.eu/coverage/): Generated unit-test coverage output.
